newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU pours money into persuading people to eat beef.
newsitem.headline: EU pours money into persuading people to eat beef.

text.p: The European Union said on Thursday it will more than double the money it spends each year to get people eating beef again.
Europeans were scared away from beef by Britain's disclosure in March last year that mad cow disease, or bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) could be passed to humans who ate infected meat.
As part of the campaign to restore confidence in beef, the European Parliament agreed to increase funds set aside for the 1997 beef promotion programme by two-thirds to 32 million ecus ($36 million).
On Thursday, EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler approved a first tranche of 11.1 million ecus ($12.6 million) for promotional schemes in 10 EU member states.
This includes two million ecus ($2.3 million) to encourage British consumers to eat more local beef, even though the EU has banned exports of British beef since March 1996.
"There's no contradiction," a Commission spokesman said, adding that the ban would be lifted when Britain had fulfilled the safety preconditions.
Nearly all the reported cases of BSE have been in Britain.
No promotional programmes were approved for Luxembourg, Greece, Finland, Denmark and Portugal.
The EU, which covers 60 percent of the cost of the programmes, pays for television, radio and newspaper advertising and participation in trade fairs.
